## Core Methodology

### The isolated-platform discoverability pattern

When the same piece of content is:
- **Visible in Tier 1** (its originating platform's in-site search) — e.g., a Bilibili video ranking 5/8 keywords at position 1
- **NOT visible in Tier 2** (cross-engine search like Google / Bing / 百度) — e.g., 0/4 probes return the URL
- **NOT visible in Tier 3** (AI-augmented search like Perplexity / Kimi / 豆包 / Claude with web) — e.g., 0% citation rate after 14 days

This is `isolated-platform discoverability` — a far more common client diagnostic profile than "content is bad" or "channel is dead." It is **diagnosable** with structured probes, and the diagnosis itself is the deliverable.

### The 4-probe × 3-engine × 6-AI-platform × query-trichotomy framework

**4 probes (cross-engine, per target URL)**:
1. `site:fully-qualified-URL` — tests whether the engine can locate the URL via site operator
2. Pure article ID in quotes — tests strictest indexing signal
3. Full title in quotes — tests exact-match indexing
4. Author + core keyword — tests author-signature indexing

**3 search engines**: Google / Bing / 百度

**6 AI search platforms**:
1. Perplexity (own crawler + real-time web)
2. Kimi 联网 (Kimi Web Search)
3. 豆包 (ByteDance own + partner sources)
4. 通义联网 (Alibaba own)
5. 秘塔 AI (own index)
6. 夸克 AI (Quark / UC index)

**Query trichotomy**:
- **Brand terms** — does this person/account exist in the citation graph?
- **Question terms** — does this content answer real user intent? (highest value)
- **Long-tail exact terms** — does the indexing system have narrow-scope recall?

**Hit detection algorithm**: strict page-level. Non-root URL must contain domain stem AND path identifier (e.g., for `zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/12345`, the citation must contain `zhihu.com` AND `12345` — not just `zhihu.com`). This is locked by 18 pinned test cases in `tests/test_basics.py::TestMentionDetectionPathStrict` + `TestPathIdentifier`.

## Posts: ChatGPT Ads Update Explainer

Series name: "ChatGPT Ads Update Explainer" / 「ChatGPT Ads 更新解读」. Author line: Stan Lu · ChatGPT Ads · Going Global / Stan Lu · ChatGPT Ads 出海投放. Sources on each post are split into three columns: OpenAI, coverage, and the author's own reading.

### 2026-11-16: Dress sellers on ChatGPT ads: a click rate 7x the ChatGPT average

URL (English, x-default): https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-11-16-chatgpt-ads-dress-product-feed-click-rate/
URL (中文): https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-11-16-chatgpt-ads-dress-product-feed-click-rate-zh/

**Direct answer**: A US special-occasion dress brand started product-feed ads on ChatGPT on November 12; in the first three days its two brands combined reached a 4.7% click rate (3.8% to 5.2% per day). The ChatGPT ads average is about 0.68% and the top quartile about 1% (Similarweb, May 2026); the Google Shopping average is about 0.86%. Cost per click of about $0.90 to $1.50 is low for ChatGPT but roughly twice Google Shopping and Meta for apparel, and three days show nothing about sales.

**Key facts (own campaign 2026-11-12 to 11-14; benchmarks retrieved 2026-11-15)**:
- Two brands combined: 4.7% click rate (total clicks over total impressions); brand A about 4.5%, brand B about 4.8%. Brand names, spend and traffic volume are not disclosed (own campaign).
- ChatGPT ads click rate: about 0.68% overall, about 1% top quartile, about 5.4% for the best performers (Similarweb, May 2026, via ppc.land and Search Engine Journal).
- Google Shopping: about 0.86% all-category average, 1.2% and up counted as strong (OwlClaw); an older apparel benchmark at 0.76% (The Ad Spend, WordStream 2018-2019 data).
- Meta fashion with $100 to $200 orders: 2.46% median click rate, 1.33% median conversion rate, about $0.50 per click (Lebesgue).
- Published ChatGPT ecommerce campaigns mostly report $1.70 to $4.40 per click (Opascope, PPC One). One Brazil campaign saw conversion rate fall 88% by week four (Marktech).
- Break-even conversion rate = cost per click x target ROAS / order value; at a $130 order that is about 0.7% to 1.2% for this campaign (author's estimate).
- Author's advice, not OpenAI's wording: use product-feed ads, one campaign per brand, set up UTM tags before launch, wait two full weeks before raising budget.

**Primary sources**:
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001268
- https://seroundtable.com/openai-chatgpt-ads-updates-42194.html
- https://ppc.land/chatgpt-ad-click-rate-gains-112-worldwide-similarweb-and-graphite-find/
- https://searchenginejournal.com/chatgpt-ad-ctr-markets-report/591384/
- https://owlclaw.com/benchmarks/google-shopping-benchmarks/
- https://lebesgue.io/facebook-ads/meta-ads-benchmarks-by-industry-and-aov

### 2026-10-29: ChatGPT Ads weekly performance emails and the new Conversions overview

URL (English, x-default): https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-10-29-chatgpt-ads-weekly-email-conversions-check/
URL (中文): https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-10-29-chatgpt-ads-weekly-email-conversions-check-zh/

**Direct answer**: Advertisers with active ChatGPT Ads campaigns now get a weekly performance email with week-over-week changes, and Ads Manager's Conversions page has a new overview. The email tells you what moved, not why; treat it as a prompt for a 10-minute check, not a verdict.

**Key facts (OpenAI email of about 2026-10-16; Help Center pages captured 2026-10-20)**:
- The new Conversions overview "stays visible across the Conversions tabs" and shows event volume and trends, the share of active campaigns optimizing for conversions, and active warnings linked to the Diagnostics tab (OpenAI email).
- Advertisers with active campaigns get a weekly summary of account performance, including week-over-week changes, with a link to full results (OpenAI email).
- Bug report and Product feedback are in the account menu in the bottom left corner of Ads Manager (OpenAI email).
- Attributed conversions take about 24-48 hours to appear; spend lags about 7-8 hours (Measure Results).
- An event that arrives but shows 0 is usually a mismatch with the campaign's conversion setting; custom event names must match exactly; "Historical events from the mismatched setup will not backfill." (Troubleshooting conversion tracking).
- "Using the weekly allowance early can stop delivery later in the week." (Troubleshooting Common Issues).
- The Ads Manager plugin can "schedule daily or weekly reviews" that "never change your account"; default window is the trailing seven completed days (Use the ChatGPT Ads Manager plugin).

**Primary sources**:
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001214-measure-results
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001513-understand-and-improve-event-quality
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001604-troubleshooting-conversion-tracking-for-chatgpt-ads
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001217
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001558-use-the-chatgpt-ads-manager-plugin
- https://www.seroundtable.com/openai-chatgpt-ads-updates-42321.html (coverage, 2026-10-19; source of the email image)

### 2026-10-22: ChatGPT Ads attribution windows and Event Quality Score

URL (English, x-default): https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-10-22-chatgpt-ads-attribution-window-event-quality/
URL (中文): https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-10-22-chatgpt-ads-attribution-window-event-quality-zh/

**Direct answer**: In ChatGPT Ads Manager, the attribution window changes only what reports count, not optimization, bidding or billing. Billing shapes delivery. The Event Quality Score checks conversion data and does not forecast results.

**Key facts (all from OpenAI Help Center pages, captured 2026-10-19)**:
- Click-through window 7, 14 or 30 days; view-through window 0 or 1 day; applies to every conversion column (Measure Results).
- "Changing the reporting window affects reporting only; it does not change campaign optimization, bidding, or billing." (Measure Results)
- Last-touch attribution, not multi-touch; a qualifying click takes credit over a view (Measure Results).
- Impression billing optimizes toward view and click conversions; click billing toward post-click conversions; objective, billing and conversion event cannot be changed after creation (Conversion-optimized Campaigns).
- Reporting delay: impressions and clicks about every 15 minutes; spend about 7-8 hours; attributed conversions about 24-48 hours (Measure Results).
- Event Quality Score: per pixel or data source, refreshed daily over seven complete calendar days; does not predict campaign performance; nine named warnings (Understand and improve event quality).
- Conversions API accepts events within the last 7 days and no more than 10 minutes in the future; this limit is separate from the attribution window (Troubleshooting conversion tracking).
- 52.7% of eligible one-day view-through conversions occurred within an hour of the matched ad impression (OpenAI Ads Blog, 2026-10-05).

**Primary sources**:
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001214-measure-results
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001409-conversion-measurement
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001604-troubleshooting-conversion-tracking-for-chatgpt-ads
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001513-understand-and-improve-event-quality
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001412-conversion-optimized-campaigns
- https://ads.openai.com/blog/more-ways-to-measure (2026-10-05)

### 2026-10-15: ChatGPT Ads October 5, 2026 update — what changed, what did not

URL (English, x-default): https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-10-15-chatgpt-ads-visual-ads-measurement-update/
URL (中文): https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-10-15-chatgpt-ads-visual-ads-measurement-update-zh/

**Direct answer**: OpenAI's October 5, 2026 ChatGPT Ads update changed two things: a visual ad format, tested in the US, and a first set of third-party measurement partners. It did not change who sees ads or who can buy.

**Key facts (all from OpenAI pages, captured 2026-10-13)**:
- Visual ads appear during image generation; US test, Free and Go users, initial group of advertisers (OpenAI blog, 2026-10-05).
- First third-party measurement partners: 3 data import (Hightouch, Tealium, LiveRamp), 10 attribution, early incrementality (Haus, Measured, WorkMagic) and brand measurement (Kantar, Cint) (OpenAI Ads Blog, 2026-10-05).
- Brand suitability: Negative Phrases for qualifying advertisers; DoubleVerify and IAS evaluation pilots.
- 52.7% of eligible one-day view-through conversions occurred within an hour of the matched ad impression (OpenAI early analysis of global campaigns, Ads Blog 2026-10-05).
- Self-serve eligibility follows the Help Center "Ads Manager Availability" list (63 markets marked Available on 2026-10-13); unchanged by the October 5 update.
- Ads show to Free and Go users only; the 1.2 billion weekly figure is all ChatGPT users, not the ad audience.

**Primary sources**:
- https://openai.com/index/new-chatgpt-ads-format-and-measurement/ (2026-10-05)
- https://ads.openai.com/blog/more-ways-to-measure (2026-10-05)
- https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-ads-expands-southeast-asia-taiwan/ (2026-09-23)
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001207-ads-in-chatgpt-the-basics
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001245-ads-manager-availability

## Case Studies (Posts)

### 2026-05-26: isolated-platform discoverability — Bilibili case

URL: https://potato-uu.github.io/posts/2026-05-26-isolated-platform-discoverability-audit/

**Subject**: A 7×24 AI stock-monitoring workflow tutorial video on Bilibili (BV1NzNgzNEwg) with a paired Zhihu long-form article published 2026-05-18.

**Setup**:
- Strict Day-0 baseline 2026-05-14 (target + control)
- Zhihu publication 2026-05-18 = real experiment Day 0
- B站→Zhihu backlink LIVE 2026-05-19
- Mid-check Day 8 = 2026-05-26
- Final audit Day 14 = 2026-06-01

**Day 8 measurement (2026-05-26)**:
- Tier 1 (Bilibili in-site search, 8 target keywords): 5 at rank 1, 6 in first screen (rank ≤ 11), 1 MISS
- Tier 2 (Google + Bing, 4 probes): 0/4 across all 4 probes both engines
- Tier 3 (6 AI platforms): pending Day 14

**Diagnosis**: classic isolated-platform discoverability. Content quality validated (Tier 1 ranking 1), but cross-engine discovery path broken.

**Plan B fallback** (high probability of triggering 2026-06-01): channel-viability memo declaring "low-weight new URL + single-video-page backlink is not viable as short-cycle AI search discoverability channel; redirect to higher-authority candidates: GitHub README + own-site sitemap / submission to indexed-high-authority sites (量子位 / 机器之心 / InfoQ) / third-party hub-page PR injection".

**Why this case study is valuable**:
- Falsified a load-bearing premise (single-platform backlink → AI citation) under 14-day cycle
- Validated 3 rounds of independent AI brutal review process (Codex CLI passes 1 and 3)
- Quantified the isolated-platform discoverability pattern with reproducible data
- Demonstrated "Sales Translation" capability for AI toB sales — translating technical audit findings into client business language

## Methodology Sources

This site's content is grounded in independently-published research, not vendor whitepapers:

1. **Princeton + IIT Delhi GEO paper** (KDD 2024, arxiv:2311.09735):
   - Authoritative citations improve AI visibility by **+115%**
   - Relevant statistics by **+33%**
   - Direct quotations from credible sources by **+43%**
   - These three tactics are burned into every post on this site

2. **Kevin Indig 2026 GEO report**:
   - New content (<3 months old) is cited by AI **3× more often** than older content
   - This validates continuous-output strategy over one-shot viral content

3. **@yaojingang geo-citation-lab** (602 prompts × 3 platforms × tens of thousands of pages):
   - Specificity (real data + clear definitions + comparisons) → **+50% impact**
   - Pure FAQ format → actually hurts citation rate
   - Sweet-spot content length: 1,000–3,000 words; high-impact pages average ~2,000 words with 10+ headings
   - ChatGPT cites few sources deeply (per-citation impact 5× Google); Perplexity casts wider (>2× sources)
   - Encyclopedia/explainer pages = 3× impact of news pages

4. **Ahrefs analysis**: cited pages have titles with higher semantic similarity to user queries; natural-language URL slugs (`/projects/pake`) cite more than opaque IDs (`/page?id=47`)

5. **SearchVIU experiment**: 5 AI systems tested — all failed to find content placed only in JSON-LD (no on-page visible text). LLMs read `<script type="application/ld+json">` as plain text without parsing schema semantics. Exception: Bing/Copilot uses JSON-LD to enrich its search index.

6. **CJR + Tow Center**: AI citation attribution is unreliable — 153 of 200 AI-generated citations had partial or complete errors. Structural work makes content easier to access accurately, but a cited fact ≠ user actually saw your exact words.

## Frequently Asked Questions (plain text, no FAQPage schema)

### Q: What is isolated-platform discoverability?

A: A state where content is visible via its originating platform's in-site search and gets algorithmic distribution there, but is NOT discoverable via cross-engine search (Google / Bing / 百度) or AI-augmented search (Perplexity / Kimi / 豆包 / 通义 / 秘塔 / 夸克). Typical signature: 5/8 keywords ranked at position 1 within the platform; 0/4 probes returning results across two major search engines. Common in Bilibili / 小红书 / 抖音 creators, SaaS product pages on subdomains, and enterprise knowledge bases — anywhere content is well-distributed within a closed perimeter but not exposed via crawlable text + authority signals.

### Q: How do you diagnose isolated-platform discoverability?

A: Run the 4-probe × 3-engine × 6-AI-platform × query-trichotomy framework. Use strict page-level hit detection (locked by 18 pinned test cases). Diagnose result patterns: if Tier 1 ✓ but Tier 2/3 ✗ across all probes, classic isolated-platform pattern. The framework is open-source at github.com/<TBD-handle>/seo-geo-audit.

### Q: Why is Bing/百度 indexing valuable for AI sales?

A: AI search platforms ingest from search engine indices, not always from primary crawl. ChatGPT search runs on Bing. Google AI Overviews use Google's own index. Perplexity also uses search APIs. If your pages are not indexed by Google or Bing, you cannot appear in AI search results from these platforms regardless of content quality. Different AI search / enterprise RAG / knowledge retrieval systems have different ingestion and citation logic — sales teams must diagnose which retrieval layer the client's content currently can or cannot reach.

### Q: What if Day 14 measurement shows 0 across all probes?

A: This triggers a Channel Viability Decision Memo (not "experiment failed"). The memo states: "This route falsifies hypothesis H1 (single-platform-low-authority backlink → AI citation in 14-day cycle). Result: not a failure of effort, but a determination of channel viability. Resources should redirect to stronger-authority discovery paths." Acceptable next-experiment candidates: own-domain site with sitemap submission to search consoles; submission to already-indexed high-authority sites; PR injection into third-party hub pages already cited by AI systems (e.g., awesome-* GitHub lists).

### Q: How does this differ from generic SEO?

A: 83% of AI Overview citations come from pages OUTSIDE the top 10 traditional search rankings. AI search rewards clear structure + reliable sourcing, not PageRank optimization. Specifically: AI prefers cited statistics over claims; encyclopedia/explainer pages over news pages by 3×; URLs with natural-language slugs over opaque IDs; English content for 83% of global citation samples. Many traditional SEO heuristics (keyword density, meta description optimization) predict less than one variable: whether the page actually answers the question the user asked.

### Q: Is JSON-LD schema useful?

A: Less than you'd think. SearchVIU tested 5 AI systems with content placed only in JSON-LD (not on visible page) — all 5 failed to find it. LLMs read JSON-LD `<script>` tags as plain text without parsing schema semantics. Confirmed useful for Bing/Copilot (enriches their search index). Keep existing JSON-LD for Bing/Copilot benefit + traditional rich results; do NOT add new types expecting ChatGPT or Claude to cite more.

### Q: Do you generate this content with AI?

A: No. All case-study data is collected via reproducible measurement scripts (open-source). All claims have primary-source citations. All conclusions have been adversarially reviewed by independent AI agents (Codex CLI passes 1 and 3) and revised based on their critiques. The audit trail itself is part of the methodology — and part of what makes this site different from AI-generated GEO content farms.
